I’d score this **6/10**. The repo is readable, compact, and has a decent focused test suite: `61 passed`. I did not find obvious command injection or unsafe shell usage. But I would **not approve as-is** because the accounting merge logic can silently corrupt results, and the datetime/reporting model is fragile.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **~220 LOC**, mostly in DB upsert semantics, timestamp normalization/querying, report DB opening behavior, validation, indexes/migration shape, and tests for those cases.

issues.description: Terminal states all share one rank, so ingest order can overwrite a newer final state with an older terminal state.
Upsert treats rows as unchanged when only state/end/elapsed match, ignoring corrected user, partition, CPU, GPU, submit/start, or exit-code values.
Timezone-aware timestamps are accepted but not normalized, which makes later text-based time comparisons incorrect across offsets.
Reports compare ISO timestamp strings lexicographically instead of using a normalized numeric or UTC time column.
All callers use a connect function that creates databases, so report/top commands silently create an empty DB when the path is wrong.
Read-only report commands open the database through the write/create path, masking configuration mistakes as empty reports.
Failure reporting only counts FAILED/TIMEOUT/OOM states and omits other Slurm failure-like terminal states such as NODE_FAIL, BOOT_FAIL, PREEMPTED, or DEADLINE.
Schema has no versioning, migration path, or indexes for reference-time report filters, which will hurt maintainability and larger datasets.
Parser accepts empty user/partition/exit-code fields and negative resource counts instead of rejecting clearly invalid accounting rows.
Default database and directory permissions rely on process umask, which may expose local accounting data on shared systems.
Project config defines tests only; there is no linting, formatting, type-checking, or CI-facing quality gate configured.
